scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Greg Walsh and I'm 38. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Greg, I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find unexpected charges. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account email address and the transaction ID associated with this charge?
Sure, my email is g.walsh@email.com and the transaction ID is TXN-99827-ABC.

Thank you for that information. I have successfully pulled up your account. I see that the cancellation request was processed on October 1st, which is indeed 34 days ago. Our standard 'Service Satisfaction Policy' (KB-402) mandates that refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the renewal date.
I understand that's the policy, but given the circumstances of my travel, is there any flexibility?

I appreciate your transparency regarding the situation. While the 30-day window is firm for automated processing, I have the authority to grant a one-time 'Loyalty Exception' for long-standing accounts like yours. I've reviewed your account history, and I am happy to override the policy in this instance.
That would be a huge help, thank you so much!

You are very welcome, Greg. I have processed the refund for the full amount of $49.99 to your original payment method. You should see the credit reflect in your bank statement within 3-5 business days. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and transaction, acknowledged the policy violation, but applied a 'Loyalty Exception' to issue a full refund.
